title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
summary: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place so each unique element appears once, maintaining their relative order.
statement: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place so each unique element appears once, maintaining their relative order. Return the count of unique elements. The first k elements of the array should contain the unique numbers in sorted order, with the rest of the array elements being ignored.
constraints: Modify nums in place so each distinct value appears once in sorted order at the front; return that prefix length k.
The judge checks both return and nums[:k]. Entries beyond k are ignored; returning a new list or only counting values is insufficient.
hints: Sorted input puts equal values next to each other.
Keep a write position for the end of the distinct prefix.
For each value, write it if the prefix is empty or its last value differs; increment write only after keeping a value.
Return the number written. The untouched tail does not matter.
editorial: Scan left-to-right and maintain a sorted distinct prefix before the write index. A value differs from the last accepted value exactly when it begins a new run. Write only those run starts. The write index never overtakes the read position, so input that remains to be processed is safe. The oracle builds a sorted set and reports both its length and contents; the judge independently observes the original input list.

tests.explanation: Return 2 and place [1,2] in nums[:2]. The third slot is ignored.
Return 5 with prefix [0,1,2,3,4]; nothing is required of the last five slots.
